calculators.platformMapping: Fully expressible today: optionPoints for the 6 categorical items; numeric band scoring for BMI and waist (min-inclusive/exclusive edge control needed at 25/30 and 94/102 & 80/88); condition DSL sex-branch for the waist bands; derived parameter for BMI = weight / pow(height_m, 2); additive aggregation; category bands (higher-is-worse) for the 5 risk tiers. No missing primitives.
calculators.realWorldPresence: MDCalc, Medscape Reference calculator, QxMD, LOINC-coded (97064-0), used by IDF and many national diabetes associations; the most widely deployed diabetes risk questionnaire in Europe.
calculators.cautions: Developed in a Finnish cohort — absolute risk percentages transfer imperfectly (HUNT 10-year observed incidence was lower: 0.4% at score 0–3 up to 25.0% at 20–26); questionnaire is freely reproduced in the literature (Finnish Diabetes Association origin) — give attribution; screening only, not a diagnosis; MDCalc renders its own A1C-screening recommendations (0–14 no routine screening; 15–20 A1C every 3–5 y; >=21 A1C annually) which are NOT the original categories — do not mix the two on one results screen without labels.

calculators.name: ADA/CDC Type 2 Diabetes (Prediabetes) Risk Test
calculators.whyRelevant: The dominant US consumer 60-second risk test (diabetes.org + CDC); high search volume, no labs needed. Tier 2 because it is US-derived (NHANES), overlaps the platform's existing IDRS audience, and ADA branding/copyright needs checking.

inputs.label: Are you a man or a woman?
If you are a woman, have you ever been diagnosed with gestational diabetes?
inputs.notes: Shown only when sex = Woman (condition DSL). Present in the deployed ADA/CDC consumer test (PMC8887991: seven questions, total 0–11) but NOT in Bang et al.'s published final model — see cautions.

inputs.label: Do you have a mother, father, sister, or brother with diabetes?
Have you ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure?
Are you physically active?
inputs.notes: Deployed consumer scoring (PMC8887991 verbatim: "a negative response was scored as 1 and a positive response was scored as 0"). Bang et al.'s underlying model instead scored active = -1; the consumer form rescaled — see cautions.

inputs.label: Weight relative to height (from the height/weight chart, equivalent to BMI category)
inputs.notes: Compute BMI from height + weight and band it: normal/underweight = 0; overweight = 1; obese = 2; extremely obese = 3 (PMC8887991 verbatim: "normal and underweight were scored as 0, overweight as 1, obese class I as 2 and obese class II as 3"; Bang et al. categories: "Not overweight or obese" 0, "Overweight" 1, "Obese" 2, "Extremely obese" 3). US chart columns correspond to standard BMI cutoffs 25 / 30 / 40 — confirm exact printed pound ranges before rendering a chart (CDC PDF was 403-blocked; see openIssues).

calculators.logic: Sum of points. Deployed consumer version: 7 items, "total score of 0–11" (max achievable 10 for either sex, since the man point and gestational-diabetes point are mutually exclusive); high risk at "five and above" (PMC8887991 verbatim: "participants who scored five and above were considered as at high-risk of developing diabetes"). Underlying model (Bang et al., Ann Intern Med 2009;151(11):775-783, via PMC3633111, verbatim): Age <40 = 0, 40–49 = 1, 50–59 = 2, >=60 = 3; Male = 1; Family history yes = 1; Hypertension yes = 1; Obesity: not overweight/obese = 0, overweight = 1, obese = 2, extremely obese = 3; Physically active yes = -1; max score 9; "We selected the cutpoint >= 5 to designate an individual as having a high risk for undiagnosed diabetes" with "sensitivity of 79%, specificity of 67%, PPV of 10%, and NPV of 99%".
calculators.outputScale: Integer 0–11 (achievable max 10); higher = higher risk of prediabetes/type 2 diabetes.

resultCategories.label: Lower risk
resultCategories.interpretation: Below the ADA/CDC high-risk threshold. This test isn't a diagnosis — only a doctor can confirm diabetes or prediabetes status (paraphrasing diabetes.org).
resultCategories.recommendation: Keep weight in a healthy range, stay physically active, and retake the test if risk factors change.

resultCategories.label: High risk for prediabetes / type 2 diabetes
resultCategories.interpretation: At the deployed threshold (score 5+) the ADA/CDC test flags increased risk of undiagnosed prediabetes/type 2 diabetes (validation at this cutpoint: sensitivity 79%, specificity 67%).
resultCategories.recommendation: See a healthcare provider for a blood test (fasting glucose, A1C, or OGTT); CDC recommends discussing enrollment in a National Diabetes Prevention Program lifestyle-change program. Not a diagnosis.

calculators.name: Metabolic Syndrome Criteria Checker (AHA/NHLBI ATP III & 2009 Harmonized)
calculators.whyRelevant: Perfect lab-report lead magnet: consumes triglycerides, HDL, fasting glucose (standard panels) plus self-measured waist and BP; produces an actionable named finding; complements the Niro CWS domains.

inputs.label: Sex
inputs.notes: Branches waist and HDL thresholds.

inputs.label: Ancestry/ethnicity (for waist-circumference threshold)

options.label: US/Canada default (AHA/NHLBI): men >=102 cm, women >=88 cm
Asian / South Asian (IDF): men >=90 cm, women >=80 cm

inputs.notes: 2009 harmonized statement makes waist cutoffs "population and country-specific" (Endotext verbatim). Only these two threshold sets are verified; do not ship additional ethnicity rows (e.g. Japanese) without verification — see openIssues.

inputs.label: Fasting triglycerides
inputs.notes: 1.7 mmol/L = 150 mg/dL (PMC11938217 quotes the criterion as ">=1.7 mmol/L"); confirm the 88.5 conversion constant against an official SI table before shipping.

inputs.label: On drug treatment for elevated triglycerides (e.g., fibrate)?
inputs.notes: "Drug treatment for elevated triglycerides, low HDL-C, hypertension, or glucose serves as alternate indicator" (Endotext, verbatim).

inputs.label: HDL cholesterol
inputs.notes: Confirm 38.67 conversion constant against an official SI table before shipping.

inputs.label: On drug treatment for reduced HDL-C?
On drug treatment for elevated glucose?

calculators.logic: Diagnosis-pattern: count how many of 5 components are met; metabolic syndrome = 3 or more (StatPearls: "3 of 5"; Endotext: "Requires 3 of 5 risk factors"). Components (AHA/NHLBI ATP III per Endotext, verbatim numbers): (1) Waist circumference >=102 cm (40 in) males; >=88 cm (35 in) females [NHLBI consumer page: "more than 40 inches" men / "more than 35 inches" women]; Asian/South Asian alternative per IDF & 2009 harmonized: >=90 cm men, >=80 cm women (PMC11938217: "the IDF for South Asians, which suggests WC thresholds of 90 cm for men and 80 cm for women"). (2) Triglycerides >=150 mg/dL (>=1.7 mmol/L) OR on drug treatment. (3) HDL-C <40 mg/dL men, <50 mg/dL women OR on drug treatment. (4) Blood pressure systolic >=130 mm Hg and/or diastolic >=85 mm Hg OR antihypertensive drug treatment (StatPearls verbatim: "systolic 130 mm Hg or higher or diastolic 85 mm Hg or higher"). (5) Fasting glucose >=100 mg/dL OR on drug treatment (NHLBI consumer framing: elevated fasting blood sugar 100–125 prediabetes, >=126 diabetes; harmonized threshold >=100). Componentcount >= 3 => meets criteria.
calculators.outputScale: Component count 0–5 plus binary meets/does-not-meet at >=3.

resultCategories.label: Criteria not met (0–2 components)
resultCategories.interpretation: Fewer than the 3 components required for metabolic syndrome. Individual elevated components still carry risk.
resultCategories.recommendation: Show which components are elevated; advise addressing each (diet, activity, weight, BP follow-up) and routine re-screening.

resultCategories.label: Meets metabolic syndrome criteria (3–5 components)
resultCategories.interpretation: Meets the AHA/NHLBI (and 2009 harmonized) definition of metabolic syndrome: 3 or more of the 5 risk components, which is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.
resultCategories.recommendation: See a healthcare provider to confirm with clinical measurements and to plan management (lifestyle change first-line; treatment of individual components per guidelines). This tool is a screening aid, not a diagnosis.

No missing primitives, but confirm the condition DSL can branch waist threshold on an ethnicity context variable.

calculators.cautions: Metabolic syndrome is a clinical diagnosis — BP must be properly measured (ideally repeated), waist measured per protocol; drug-treatment alternate indicators must be asked or the count under-detects; ethnic waist cutoffs beyond the two verified sets (e.g. Japan-specific) are NOT verified here; surface AHA/NHLBI vs IDF/harmonized as labeled alternatives, never merged. No licensing restrictions on criteria.

calculators.name: OGTT 2-Hour Glucose Interpreter (75-g, ADA categories)
calculators.whyRelevant: Direct lab-report interpreter (OGTT and fasting glucose values appear on lab PDFs); trivially implementable; anchors the prediabetes content cluster alongside IDRS and FINDRISC.

inputs.label: 2-hour plasma glucose (75-g oral glucose tolerance test)
Fasting plasma glucose (optional, for combined interpretation)

calculators.logic: ADA categories, verbatim from diabetes.org: OGTT 2-hour glucose — Normal: "less than 140 mg/dL"; Prediabetes: "140 to 199 mg/dL"; Diabetes: "200 mg/dL or higher". Fasting plasma glucose — Normal: "less than 100 mg/dL"; Prediabetes: "100 mg/dl to 125 mg/dL"; Diabetes: "126 mg/dL or higher". Random plasma glucose diabetes threshold: "greater than or equal to 200 mg/dL". A1C for context: Normal "less than 5.7%", Prediabetes "5.7% to 6.4%", Diabetes "6.5% or higher". If both fasting and 2-h values are given, report the more advanced category.
calculators.outputScale: Categorical: Normal / Prediabetes (impaired glucose tolerance) / In the diabetes range.

resultCategories.label: Normal glucose tolerance
resultCategories.interpretation: 2-hour value below the ADA prediabetes threshold.
resultCategories.recommendation: Maintain healthy lifestyle; re-screen per age/risk-based guidance.

resultCategories.label: Prediabetes (impaired glucose tolerance)
resultCategories.interpretation: Within the ADA prediabetes range for the 2-hour OGTT.
resultCategories.recommendation: Discuss with a healthcare provider; structured lifestyle change (weight loss, activity) substantially lowers progression risk; retesting per provider guidance.

resultCategories.label: In the diabetes range
resultCategories.interpretation: Meets the ADA 2-hour OGTT threshold for diabetes; diagnosis requires clinical confirmation (typically a second abnormal test).
resultCategories.recommendation: See a healthcare provider promptly for confirmatory testing and management. This tool does not diagnose.

calculators.platformMapping: Fully expressible today: numeric band scoring with min-inclusive edges (140/200, 100/126), max() aggregation to take the more advanced of the fasting and 2-hour categories, category bands higher-is-worse. No missing primitives.
calculators.realWorldPresence: Thresholds implemented on virtually every lab-results portal and hospital patient education page; ADA/CDC/NIDDK all publish the identical table.
calculators.cautions: Interpreter only — ADA requires confirmatory testing for diagnosis in the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia; GESTATIONAL diabetes OGTT uses entirely different thresholds and protocols (excluded — state this on-page); values assume a properly conducted 75-g OGTT with plasma glucose.

calculators.name: TyG Index (Triglyceride-Glucose Index)
calculators.whyRelevant: Insulin-resistance surrogate computable from a standard lipid panel + fasting glucose (no insulin assay needed) — ideal for the lab-report lead magnet; rapidly growing search interest. Requires ln() engine primitive.
calculators.logic: TyG = ln[fasting triglycerides (mg/dL) x fasting plasma glucose (mg/dL) / 2] — natural log, division by 2 INSIDE the log. Verbatim from PMC9502283: "Ln [fasting triglycerides (mg/dL) x fasting plasma glucose (mg/dL)/2]"; PMC6963998 identical. Original derivation: Simental-Mendia LE et al., Metab Syndr Relat Disord 2008;6(4):299-304. CRITICAL SCALE AMBIGUITY: a second variant, [ln(TG x glucose)]/2 (division OUTSIDE the log), circulates in the literature and yields values ~4.5–5.0 instead of ~8–10; the Guerrero-Romero 2010 clamp-validation cutoff of 4.68 (sensitivity 96.5%, specificity 85.0%, AUC 0.858, per search-verified summaries of JCEM 2010;95(7):3347-3351 and the Sanchez-Garcia 2020 systematic review) is on that half-log scale and MUST NOT be applied to the ln[TG x G/2] output. Cutoffs verified on the ln[TG x G/2] scale (PMC9502283, verbatim): TyG >= 9.04 intermediate/high cardiovascular risk (Brazil cohort, sens 62.5%, spec 66.7%); >9.0 adverse events post-STEMI (Luo 2019, AUC 0.685); 9.323 MACE in diabetes with ACS (Wang 2020); 9.04 predicted coronary artery calcification progression (Lee & Kang 2019).
calculators.outputScale: Unitless (ln scale); with the standard ln[TG x G/2] formula, typical adult values roughly 7.5–10.5; higher = more insulin resistant / higher cardiometabolic risk.

resultCategories.label: No elevated-risk signal (cited cohorts)
resultCategories.interpretation: Below the ~9.0 cutoffs associated with elevated cardiovascular risk in the cited study populations. No consensus general-population 'normal' exists.
resultCategories.recommendation: Use as a tracking metric alongside standard lipid and glucose targets; maintain healthy lifestyle.

resultCategories.label: Elevated (associated with cardiometabolic risk in studies)
resultCategories.interpretation: At/above cutoffs (9.0–9.32 across cited cohorts) associated with intermediate/high cardiovascular risk or adverse events in specific study populations; also consistent with insulin resistance as TyG rises.
resultCategories.recommendation: Discuss triglycerides, glucose, and overall cardiometabolic risk with a healthcare provider; address diet, activity, and weight. Screening signal only — cutoffs are population-specific, not diagnostic.

Formula-scale and study-specific cutoff choices, source verification, population applicability, and clinical review remain unresolved; do not author or publish from this research row.
calculators.realWorldPresence: mdapp.co and numerous clinical/wellness calculators; heavily used in recent cardiometabolic literature (hundreds of cohort papers); appearing on consumer longevity/lab-interpretation platforms.
calculators.cautions: Two incompatible formula scales circulate (ln[TG*G/2] ~8-10 vs [ln(TG*G)]/2 ~4.5-5) — implement ln[TG*G/2] and display only same-scale cutoffs; no consensus diagnostic cutoff for the general population (present thresholds as study-specific reference points with population labels); requires fasting sample; triglycerides are volatile (recent alcohol/food); not validated as a diagnostic test. Public-domain formula.

calculators.name: eGFR & CKD Stage (CKD-EPI 2021 + KDIGO G/A staging)
calculators.whyRelevant: Flagship kidney calculator; eGFR is on virtually every metabolic lab panel, making this a core lab-report lead-magnet tool. Pairs directly with the existing Niro CWS biomarker flow. The 2021 race-free equation is the current NKF/ASN-recommended standard.

inputs.label: Age
inputs.notes: Equation developed/validated in adults. Do not allow <18 (pediatric equations differ — out of scope).

inputs.label: Serum creatinine (standardized/IDMS-calibrated)
inputs.notes: µmol/L → mg/dL: divide by 88.4 (factor 0.011312). Conversion factor derived from MedlinePlus paired ranges: men 0.7–1.3 mg/dL = 62–115 µmol/L.

calculators.logic: VERBATIM (kidney.org, professionals/kdoqi/gfr_calculator/formula): 'eGFR = 142 * min(standardized Scr/K, 1)^α * max(standardized Scr/K, 1)^-1.200 * 0.9938^Age * 1.012 [if female]' where K = 0.7 (females) or 0.9 (males); α = -0.241 (females) or -0.302 (males). CONFIRMED against primary paper (Inker et al., NEJM 2021, via PMC8822996, Table 2): intercept 142; kappa 0.7 female / 0.9 male; alpha1 (Scr ≤ kappa) female −0.241, male −0.302; alpha2 (Scr > kappa) −1.200 (applies to both sexes); age coefficient 0.9938^Age; female sex coefficient 1.012. Output unit: mL/min/1.73 m². Piecewise behavior is fully encoded by the min()/max() construction: when Scr/κ ≤ 1 only the min-term is <1 (raised to α) and the max-term is 1; when Scr/κ > 1 the min-term is 1 and the max-term is raised to −1.200.
calculators.outputScale: eGFR in mL/min/1.73 m², typically ~2 to ~150; report rounded to whole number; values ≥90 are in the normal range (NKF)

resultCategories.label: G1 — Normal or high (only CKD if kidney-damage markers present)
resultCategories.interpretation: NKF: 'eGFR of 90 or higher is in the normal range' — normal filtering function (90–100%). G1 CKD is only diagnosed when eGFR ≥90 is accompanied by evidence of kidney damage (e.g., albuminuria) persisting ≥3 months.
resultCategories.recommendation: A result in this range is reassuring on its own. Keep up routine checkups; if you also have protein/albumin in the urine, diabetes, or high blood pressure, discuss kidney health monitoring with your clinician.

resultCategories.label: G2 — Mildly decreased
resultCategories.interpretation: Mild loss of kidney function (NKF: 60–89%). By KDIGO definition this is NOT CKD unless kidney-damage markers (e.g., albuminuria) are also present for ≥3 months.
resultCategories.recommendation: Often normal for age. Share the result with your clinician, especially if you have diabetes, hypertension, or a family history of kidney disease; a urine albumin (ACR) test completes the picture.

resultCategories.label: G3a — Mildly to moderately decreased
resultCategories.interpretation: Mild-to-moderate loss of kidney function; if persistent ≥3 months this meets the CKD definition (eGFR <60 regardless of damage markers — StatPearls/KDIGO).
resultCategories.recommendation: See your clinician to confirm with a repeat test and a urine ACR. Management focuses on blood pressure and blood sugar control and reviewing medicines that affect kidneys. CKD usually has no symptoms at this stage — early detection matters (NKF).

resultCategories.label: G3b — Moderately to severely decreased
resultCategories.interpretation: Moderate-to-severe loss of kidney function (NKF: 30–44%).
resultCategories.recommendation: Medical follow-up is important; your clinician may check for complications (anemia, bone/mineral changes) and consider nephrology referral per KDIGO-based practice.

resultCategories.label: G4 — Severely decreased
resultCategories.interpretation: Severe loss of kidney function (NKF: 15–29%).
resultCategories.recommendation: Nephrologist care is typically needed at this stage, including planning for possible future kidney-failure treatment. Do not delay follow-up.

resultCategories.label: G5 — Kidney failure
resultCategories.interpretation: NKF: 'eGFR below 15 may mean kidney failure'; KDIGO G5 is GFR <15 or treatment by dialysis (StatPearls).
resultCategories.recommendation: This result requires prompt medical care. Treatment options (dialysis, transplant) are decisions made with a nephrology team.

Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) — stage interpretation
Creatinine blood test (unit conversion basis: mg/dL ↔ µmol/L)

calculators.platformMapping: Derived parameter: egfr = 142 * pow(min(scr/kappa, 1), alpha) * pow(max(scr/kappa, 1), -1.200) * pow(0.9938, age) * (sex=='female' ? 1.012 : 1). kappa and alpha resolved via ternary or condition DSL on sex (kappa = sex=='female' ? 0.7 : 0.9; alpha = sex=='female' ? -0.241 : -0.302). Staging via numeric band scoring on the derived eGFR (min-inclusive edges: 90, 60, 45, 30, 15), direction higher-is-better; unit conversion factor for µmol/L input. ENGINE CAPABILITY AVAILABLE: engine v1 supports finite fractional and negative pow(), min/max, and condition branches, so the formula shape is structurally expressible. Source, applicability, unit, staging, and clinical review remain required before authoring or publication.
calculators.realWorldPresence: NKF eGFR calculator (kidney.org), MDCalc 'CKD-EPI Equations for Glomerular Filtration Rate', Medscape calculators, NIDDK/NKDEP professional tools — the standard consumer & clinical eGFR tool everywhere since the 2021 NKF-ASN task force recommendation.
calculators.cautions: Estimate only — not valid for people under 18, during pregnancy, in acute kidney injury/rapidly changing creatinine, or at extremes of muscle mass (bodybuilders, amputation, malnutrition, creatine supplements — StatPearls). Requires standardized (IDMS-calibrated) creatinine. Educational disclaimer required: does not diagnose CKD (diagnosis needs persistence ≥3 months and clinical context). Equation itself is published in the open literature — no licensing restriction.

mergedFrom.name: CKD Stage & Risk Classifier (KDIGO G × A heat map)
mergedFrom.whyRelevant: Turns two common lab values (eGFR + urine ACR) into the exact KDIGO stage and 4-level prognosis risk category — the standard clinical framework, highly shareable as a lab-report explainer, and a natural chained output of the eGFR calculator.

inputs.label: eGFR
inputs.notes: Can be piped from the ckd-epi-2021-egfr calculator (derived input) or entered from a lab report.

inputs.label: Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR)
inputs.notes: mg/mmol → mg/g multiply by 8.84 (1 g creatinine = 8.84 mmol). Optional: allow 'not tested' → classify G stage only, no risk matrix.

mergedFrom.logic: G CATEGORIES (kidney.org 'How to Classify CKD', verbatim ranges in mL/min/1.73 m²): G1 ≥90 'Normal or high'; G2 60–89 'Mildly decreased'; G3a 45–59 'Mildly to moderately decreased'; G3b 30–44 'Moderately to severely decreased'; G4 15–29 'Severely decreased'; G5 <15 'Kidney failure' (StatPearls adds: 'or treatment by dialysis'). A CATEGORIES (kidney.org): A1 ACR <30 mg/g 'Normal to mildly increased'; A2 30–300 mg/g 'Moderately increased'; A3 >300 mg/g 'Severely increased'. StatPearls (NBK535404) gives mg/mmol equivalents: A1 '<3.4 mg/mmol', A2 '3.4-34 mg/mmol', A3 '>34 mg/mmol'; NHS/NICE convention uses rounded 3 and 30 mg/mmol — CONFLICT recorded, surface both. CKD DEFINITION (StatPearls verbatim): 'kidney damage or an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of less than 60 mL/min/1.73 m², persisting for 3 months or more.' RISK MATRIX (KDIGO 2012 heat map, confirmed via PMC7854398 systematic review + PMC4709677): LOW/green = G1A1, G2A1; MODERATELY INCREASED/yellow = G1A2, G2A2, G3aA1; HIGH/orange = G1A3, G2A3, G3aA2, G3bA1; VERY HIGH/red = G3aA3, G3bA2, G3bA3, all G4 (A1–A3), all G5 (A1–A3).
mergedFrom.outputScale: Composite stage label 'G{1|2|3a|3b|4|5} A{1|2|3}' plus one of 4 risk categories (low / moderately increased / high / very high)

resultCategories.label: Low risk (green)
resultCategories.interpretation: Normal-to-mildly-reduced eGFR with normal-to-mildly-increased albuminuria. By KDIGO definition, no CKD unless other kidney-damage markers persist ≥3 months.
resultCategories.recommendation: Routine health maintenance; recheck as advised, particularly if you have diabetes or high blood pressure.

resultCategories.label: Moderately increased risk (yellow)
resultCategories.interpretation: Either moderately increased albuminuria with preserved eGFR, or mildly-moderately reduced eGFR with normal albuminuria. Elevated albuminuria is one of the most important predictors of CKD progression and cardiovascular risk (PMC).
resultCategories.recommendation: Confirm with repeat testing (persistence ≥3 months defines CKD) and discuss monitoring frequency, blood-pressure and glucose control with your clinician.

resultCategories.label: High risk (orange)
resultCategories.interpretation: Severely increased albuminuria and/or moderately reduced kidney function — high risk of CKD progression, kidney failure and cardiovascular events.
resultCategories.recommendation: Medical follow-up is needed. Management typically includes blood-pressure control, diabetes management, medication review; nephrology input may be considered.

resultCategories.label: Very high risk (red)
resultCategories.range: G3aA3, G3bA2, G3bA3, G4 (any A), G5 (any A)
resultCategories.interpretation: Advanced CKD and/or heavy albuminuria — very high risk of progression to kidney failure.
resultCategories.recommendation: Prompt nephrology care. At G4–G5 this includes complication screening and planning for kidney-failure treatment options.

mergedFrom.platformMapping: G stage: numeric bands on eGFR (edges 90/60/45/30/15, min-inclusive control needed at each boundary — KDIGO ranges are inclusive at the lower edge, e.g., G2 = 60–89). A stage: numeric bands on ACR mg/g (edges 30 and 300; note kidney.org writes A2 as 30–300 and A3 as >300 while StatPearls writes A2 as 30–299 — set band edges 30 inclusive / 300 exclusive-upper and record the discrepancy). Risk category: 6×3 = 18-cell matrix — this is a 2-D LOOKUP. If the engine lookup primitive is strictly 1-D (points→value), either (a) MISSING PRIMITIVE: composite-key lookup ('G3a|A2'→risk) or 2-D table support, or (b) express as nested condition-DSL branches (18 branches — expressible today but verbose/config-heavy). Unit conversion factor 8.84 for mg/mmol→mg/g.
mergedFrom.realWorldPresence: MDCalc 'CKD staging with KDIGO criteria', QxMD Calculate, embedded in every nephrology EHR flowsheet; the G×A heat map is reproduced in NKF, NICE, and primary-care CKD guidance worldwide.
mergedFrom.cautions: Staging requires PERSISTENCE ≥3 months — a single lab value never diagnoses CKD; surface this prominently. A single elevated ACR can be transient (exercise, fever, UTI). The risk matrix values were confirmed from peer-reviewed PMC articles because the KDIGO primary PDF returned 403 (see openIssues). KDIGO framework is openly published; no instrument licensing issues.

calculators.mergeNote: KDIGO G/A staging and the G-by-A risk heat-map are integrated; optional ACR input adds the A stage (see mergedFrom). Eliminates the previously duplicated G-band table.

calculators.name: Creatinine Clearance (Cockcroft-Gault)
calculators.whyRelevant: Historically the standard for drug-dose adjustment and still requested/searched; however NKF now explicitly advocates transitioning away from it toward race-agnostic eGFR, so it is a catalog/completeness tool, not a launch flagship. Useful SEO pairing next to the eGFR calculator with an honest 'why these differ' explainer.
calculators.logic: VERBATIM (StatPearls 'Creatinine Clearance', NBK544228): 'CrCl = [(140 – Age) × Mass (kg) × 0.85 if female] / 72 × [Serum Creatinine (mg/dL)]' — i.e., CrCl (mL/min) = (140 − age) × weight(kg) / (72 × Scr mg/dL), multiplied by 0.85 if female. Primary citation: Cockcroft DW, Gault MH. Prediction of creatinine clearance from serum creatinine. Nephron. 1976;16(1):31-41 (search-verified; original formula 'in adult males (15% less in females)'). Output is mL/min, NOT normalized to 1.73 m². Normal young-adult values (StatPearls): 'about 100 to 120 mL/min in males and 90 to 110 mL/min in females'.
calculators.outputScale: CrCl in mL/min (absolute, not body-surface normalized); typical healthy young adult ~90–120 mL/min

resultCategories.label: Within typical young-adult range
resultCategories.range: Male ≥100 mL/min; Female ≥90 mL/min (StatPearls: normal ~100–120 M / 90–110 F)
resultCategories.interpretation: Estimated creatinine clearance in the range seen in younger healthy adults. Note CrCl overestimates true GFR by approximately 10% to 20% because creatinine is also secreted by peritubular capillaries (StatPearls).
resultCategories.recommendation: No action implied by this estimate alone. For kidney-health staging, use the eGFR (CKD-EPI 2021) result instead.

resultCategories.label: Below typical range
resultCategories.interpretation: Estimated clearance below the typical young-adult range. Clearance normally declines with age, and this equation's accuracy is reduced at higher body weights/BMI (NKF) and in altered muscle mass (StatPearls).
resultCategories.recommendation: Interpretation and any medication dose adjustment belong to your clinician/pharmacist — this number is historically used for drug dosing, and NKF now recommends transitioning to modern eGFR equations. Cross-check with the CKD-EPI 2021 eGFR calculator and discuss results with a professional.

Unit conversion factors for lb→kg (0.453592) and µmol/L→mg/dL (0.011312). Sex-split category bands via condition DSL. NO missing primitives.
calculators.realWorldPresence: MDCalc 'Creatinine Clearance (Cockcroft-Gault Equation)', Medscape/reference.medscape.com CrCl calculator, historically embedded in every pharmacy dosing reference; kidney.org hosts a dedicated explainer on its limitations.
calculators.cautions: NKF verbatim criticisms to surface: 'Developed with data from 249 white males, with the 15% adjustment for females estimated rather than scientifically quantified' and it predates standardized creatinine assays; 'use of total body weight... across the body size or weight spectrum reduces C-G eCrCL accuracy.' Which weight to use in obesity (ideal/adjusted body weight) is practice-dependent and was NOT verifiable from our allowed sources — do not embed an IBW rule without sourcing it (see openIssues). Not for <18, pregnancy, unstable creatinine. Educational-use disclaimer; dosing decisions are clinician/pharmacist territory.

calculators.name: BUN:Creatinine Ratio Calculator
calculators.whyRelevant: Both values appear on every basic/comprehensive metabolic panel; the ratio is a classic lab-report question ('is my high BUN from dehydration?'). Trivial math, high search volume, perfect lab-report lead-magnet companion.

inputs.label: Blood urea nitrogen (BUN)
inputs.notes: Urea mmol/L → BUN mg/dL: multiply by 2.801 (derived from NCBI Clinical Methods verbatim pairing '5 to 20 mg/dl, or 1.8 to 7.1 mmol urea per liter'). Ratio thresholds below assume conventional US units (mg/dL both).

calculators.logic: Ratio = BUN (mg/dL) ÷ serum creatinine (mg/dL). THRESHOLDS (StatPearls 'Prerenal Kidney Failure', NBK560678, verbatim): normal — 'Typically, this ratio is 10'; prerenal disease — 'in prerenal disease, it is higher than 20:1'; acute tubular necrosis — 'in ATN, it is about 15:1'. Mechanism (verbatim): 'This occurs secondary to the passive reabsorption of urea in the proximal tubules, which follows the proximal tubule reabsorption of sodium and water that occurs in prerenal disease.' Corroborating StatPearls sources (search-verified): ratio '>20:1 in prerenal disease and <10:1 in renal diseases'; '>20:1 suggests a prerenal cause, such as dehydration or reduced renal perfusion.' Low-ratio causes (NCBI Clinical Methods NBK305, verbatim): 'A low BUN/Cr ratio suggests inadequate protein intake, reduced urea synthesis as in advanced liver disease, supernormal excretion of urea as in sickle cell anemia, increased creatinine production as in rhabdomyolysis.' High-ratio non-renal drivers (NBK305): high protein intake, gastrointestinal bleeding, liver disease [as extrarenal factors raising BUN]. Component normals: BUN 5–20 mg/dL (NBK305) / adult female 6–21, adult male 8–24, children 1–17: 7–20 mg/dL (Cleveland Clinic); creatinine male 0.6–1.2, female 0.5–1.1 mg/dL (NBK305, enzymatic).
calculators.outputScale: Dimensionless ratio, typically ~5–40; displayed as 'X:1'

resultCategories.label: Low ratio
resultCategories.interpretation: Ratio below the typical ~10:1. Can reflect low protein intake, reduced urea synthesis (advanced liver disease), increased urea excretion (e.g., sickle cell anemia), or increased creatinine production (e.g., rhabdomyolysis) — per NCBI Clinical Methods. Intrinsic renal disease can also lower the ratio (StatPearls).
resultCategories.recommendation: A low ratio alone is rarely meaningful — interpret with the absolute BUN and creatinine values and your clinical context; discuss with your clinician if either absolute value is out of range.

resultCategories.label: Typical ratio
resultCategories.interpretation: Within the usual range (StatPearls: normal is typically about 10; values up to 20:1 are conventionally considered unremarkable when BUN and creatinine are individually normal). Note ~15:1 is also described in ATN — the ratio cannot exclude kidney disease.
resultCategories.recommendation: No action implied by the ratio itself. Check whether BUN and creatinine are each within their reference ranges.

resultCategories.label: Elevated ratio (prerenal pattern)
resultCategories.interpretation: StatPearls: 'in prerenal disease, it is higher than 20:1' — classically dehydration or reduced kidney blood flow. But BUN also rises independently with high protein intake, GI bleeding, and certain medications (Clinical Methods/Cleveland Clinic), so an elevated ratio is a pattern, not a diagnosis.
resultCategories.recommendation: If you may be dehydrated, rehydrate sensibly and retest per your clinician's advice. If creatinine is also elevated or you feel unwell, seek medical review — providers never use BUN alone to define kidney problems (Cleveland Clinic).

sources.title: Prerenal Kidney Failure (NBK560678) — ratio thresholds 10 / ~15:1 ATN / >20:1 prerenal + mechanism
BUN and Creatinine (NBK305) — normal ranges, low/high ratio causes, BUN variability caveat
Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) Test — age/sex-specific BUN reference ranges, 'BUN alone' caveat

calculators.platformMapping: Fully expressible: derived parameter ratio = bun / scr (both normalized to mg/dL via unit conversion factors 2.801 and 0.011312); category bands on the derived ratio (edges 10 and 20, min-inclusive control). Optional secondary flags (BUN out-of-range, creatinine out-of-range) via additional bands with condition DSL for sex-specific creatinine ranges. NO missing primitives.
calculators.realWorldPresence: MDCalc 'BUN Creatinine Ratio', lab-explainer pages at Cleveland Clinic and testing.com-class sites; commonly auto-reported on Quest/Labcorp panels.
calculators.cautions: This ratio is a screening pattern, NOT a diagnosis — NBK305 stresses BUN is 'far more variable than sCr due to diet, hydration, and metabolic factors.' Ratio conventions assume US conventional units; SI-entered values must be converted first (engine handles this — never compute urea:creatinine in SI and compare to 10/20 thresholds, the SI urea:creatinine convention uses different cutoffs). Conservative disclaimer + 'see a clinician if values abnormal' required.

calculators.name: Daily Water & Fluid Intake Guide
calculators.whyRelevant: Massive wellness search volume ('how much water should I drink'); zero-risk lead magnet that fits the hydration side of the category. Honest version is a guideline lookup, not a pseudo-precise formula — which differentiates Niro from mL/kg myth calculators.

inputs.label: Age
inputs.notes: AI values sourced for adults 19+; do not serve pediatric values (not sourced).

inputs.label: Pregnancy/lactation status
inputs.notes: Only shown when sex=female (condition DSL).

inputs.label: Conditions today

options.label: Prolonged physical activity / hot weather / illness

inputs.notes: Drives qualitative 'you may need more' messaging only — no sourced quantitative增量 exists in allowed sources; do NOT invent one.

calculators.logic: US NATIONAL ACADEMIES / IOM 2005 ADEQUATE INTAKE (total water = beverages + drinking water + food moisture), verbatim via PMC7692653: men (19–30 y) '3.7 L (131 oz)' per day; women '2.7 L (95 oz)/day'; ages 31–50 AI 'is set equal to that for younger adults'. 'Approximately 80 percent of total water intake comes from drinking beverages and water' (≈2.96 L beverages for men, ≈2.16 L for women — derived, label as derived). MedlinePlus corroboration (verbatim): 'The Dietary Reference Intake for water is between 91 and 125 fluid ounces (2.7 to 3.7 liters) of water per day for adults'; practical guidance verbatim: 'If you drink fluids when you feel thirsty and have beverages with meals, you should get enough water to keep you hydrated.' PREGNANCY/LACTATION (IOM AI, search-verified via PMC3929375): pregnancy 3.0 L/day total water (~2.3 L / 10 cups as beverages); lactation 3.8 L/day — mark as search-verified, weaker verification tier. NHS GUIDANCE (fetch-verified, verbatim): '6 to 8 cups or glasses of fluid a day'; 'Water, lower-fat milk and sugar-free drinks, including tea and coffee, all count'; more fluid needed if 'pregnant, breastfeeding, in hot conditions, physically active for extended periods, or ill'; urine target 'a clear pale yellow colour'; 'Limit fruit juice and smoothies to a maximum of one small glass (150ml) a day'; 'Do not have more than 200mg of caffeine a day if you're pregnant.' CRITICAL: US AI (total water incl. food) and NHS cups (drinks only) are DIFFERENT CONSTRUCTS — display side-by-side labeled by org, never merged or averaged.
calculators.outputScale: Target displayed as L/day and fl oz/day (US National Academies AI, total water) alongside NHS cups/day (fluids); L → fl oz factor 33.814

resultCategories.label: Adult man (19+)
resultCategories.range: US National Academies AI: 3.7 L (131 oz)/day total water; ~80% from beverages (≈3.0 L). NHS: 6–8 cups/glasses of fluid daily.
resultCategories.interpretation: AI is total water from all sources including ~20% from food; it is an adequate-intake benchmark for generally healthy people, not a minimum you must force.
resultCategories.recommendation: Drink when thirsty and with meals (MedlinePlus); water, lower-fat milk and sugar-free drinks including tea and coffee all count (NHS); aim for pale-yellow urine; drink more during long activity, heat, or illness.

resultCategories.label: Adult woman (19+), not pregnant/breastfeeding
resultCategories.range: US National Academies AI: 2.7 L (95 oz)/day total water; ~80% from beverages (≈2.2 L). NHS: 6–8 cups/glasses of fluid daily.
resultCategories.interpretation: Same construct notes as above.
resultCategories.recommendation: Same practical guidance; limit fruit juice/smoothies to one 150 ml glass a day (NHS).

resultCategories.label: Pregnancy
resultCategories.range: IOM AI: 3.0 L/day total water (~2.3 L as beverages) [search-verified]. NHS: more fluid needed than usual; caffeine max 200 mg/day.
resultCategories.interpretation: Fluid needs rise in pregnancy; the pregnancy-specific AI value carries a weaker verification tier in our dataset (see openIssues).
resultCategories.recommendation: Follow your antenatal team's advice; keep caffeine under 200 mg/day (NHS) and prioritize water/lower-sugar drinks.

resultCategories.label: Breastfeeding
resultCategories.range: IOM AI: 3.8 L/day total water [search-verified]. NHS: more fluid needed than usual.
resultCategories.interpretation: Lactation substantially increases water needs.
resultCategories.recommendation: Drink to thirst — many find a drink alongside each feed practical; seek clinician advice for individual needs.

sources.verification: blocked-cited (HTTP 403; equivalent values verified via PMC + MedlinePlus)

calculators.platformMapping: Fully expressible: condition DSL on sex/status/age selects a lookup row (AI value); no numeric formula at all. Unit display conversion L→fl oz (33.814) and L→cups if desired. Qualitative 'increase intake' messaging is category text keyed off the context select. NO missing primitives. Deliberately NOT implemented: body-weight-based (mL/kg) intake formulas — no allowed-source basis exists; shipping one would fabricate precision.
calculators.realWorldPresence: Mayo Clinic's water article is the canonical consumer reference; CDC 'Water and Healthier Drinks' page; countless wellness apps/calculators (most use unsourced mL/kg rules — a differentiation point).
calculators.cautions: AI values are for generally healthy people — fluid RESTRICTION applies in heart failure, advanced CKD/dialysis, hyponatremia and other conditions; the tool must state that people with kidney, heart, or liver conditions should follow their clinician's fluid advice, and that overhydration is possible. US total-water AI vs NHS drinks-only guidance must remain visibly separate constructs (labeled per org). Pregnancy/lactation values are search-verified only (openIssues).

calculators.name: FIB-4 Index (Fibrosis-4) for Liver Fibrosis
calculators.whyRelevant: Highest-value liver calculator for a lab-report lead magnet: computed entirely from age + 3 values present on routine CMP/CBC panels (AST, ALT, platelets), and it is the AASLD-endorsed first-line risk stratifier for the ~30% of adults with MASLD/NAFLD. Directly complements Niro CWS biomarkers.

inputs.label: Age
inputs.notes: Score less reliable <35 and >65 (MDCalc caution, fetch-verified); AASLD: low accuracy under 35, alternate cutoff over 65.

inputs.label: AST (aspartate aminotransferase)
inputs.notes: µkat/L to U/L: multiply by 60 (MedlinePlus gives 8-33 U/L = 0.13-0.55 µkat/L).

inputs.label: Platelet count
inputs.notes: ×10⁹/L numerically equals ×10³/µL (thousand per microliter).

calculators.logic: FORMULA (verbatim, Sterling 2006 abstract): FIB-4 = age ([yr] × AST [U/L]) / ((PLT [10⁹/L]) × (ALT [U/L])^(1/2)). WHO 2024 Box 4.1 verbatim restatement: 'FIB-4 = (age (years) × AST (IU/L))/(platelet count (10⁹/L) × [ALT (IU/L)]^1/2)'. NOTE: denominator uses SQUARE ROOT of ALT. CUTOFFS — MASLD/NAFLD primary-care pathway (AASLD 2023, fetch-verified): FIB-4 <1.3 = low risk (manage in primary care); 1.3–2.67 = indeterminate (secondary assessment with elastography/ELF); FIB-4 >2.67 = 'Direct referral to gastroenterology/hepatology should be considered ... due to the increased risk of clinically significant fibrosis'. 'In patients older than age 65, a FIB-4 cutoff of >2.0 should be used' (as the low cutoff). 'FIB-4 has low accuracy in those under age 35; thus, secondary assessment should be considered.' Repeat testing: every 2–3 years if no prediabetes and 1–2 metabolic risk factors; every 1–2 years if prediabetes/T2DM or ≥2 metabolic risk factors. CUTOFFS — chronic HCV (verbatim from abstracts): Sterling 2006 validation: cutoff <1.45 NPV 90% to exclude advanced fibrosis (Ishak 4–6), sensitivity 70%; cutoff >3.25 PPV 65%, specificity 97%. Vallet-Pichard 2007 (HCV-monoinfected, n=847): FIB-4 <1.45 NPV 94.7% to exclude severe fibrosis, sensitivity 74.3%; FIB-4 >3.25 PPV 82.1% for significant fibrosis (F3–F4), specificity 98.2%; 72.8% of biopsies correctly classified using these ranges.
calculators.outputScale: Continuous positive value, typically ~0.2 to >10; interpreted against context-specific cutoffs (round display to 2 decimals).

resultCategories.label: Low risk of advanced fibrosis
resultCategories.interpretation: Advanced liver fibrosis is unlikely; AASLD guidance considers this group suitable for management in primary care.
resultCategories.recommendation: Maintain follow-up with your usual clinician. Per AASLD guidance, low-risk individuals are typically re-checked every 2–3 years, or every 1–2 years if you have prediabetes/type 2 diabetes or 2 or more metabolic risk factors. This screening estimate does not replace medical evaluation.

resultCategories.label: Indeterminate risk
resultCategories.interpretation: The result cannot rule advanced fibrosis in or out; AASLD guidance recommends a secondary assessment (e.g., liver stiffness by elastography or ELF blood test).
resultCategories.recommendation: Share this result with your clinician and ask whether a second-line test such as FibroScan (elastography) or the ELF test is appropriate for you.

resultCategories.label: High risk of clinically significant fibrosis
resultCategories.interpretation: AASLD guidance states direct referral to gastroenterology/hepatology should be considered at this level due to increased risk of clinically significant fibrosis.
resultCategories.recommendation: See a clinician promptly and discuss referral to a liver specialist. A high FIB-4 is not a diagnosis — confirmatory testing is required.

resultCategories.label: Age under 35 — result unreliable
resultCategories.interpretation: AASLD guidance: FIB-4 has low accuracy under age 35, so a low score cannot be used for reassurance.
resultCategories.recommendation: Discuss liver-health concerns with a clinician; a secondary assessment should be considered rather than relying on FIB-4.

calculators.platformMapping: derived parameter: fib4 = (age * ast) / (platelets * pow(alt, 0.5)). ENGINE CAPABILITY AVAILABLE: engine v1 supports sqrt() and finite fractional pow(), so the formula shape is structurally expressible. Unit conversion factors for AST/ALT (µkat/L ×60) and platelets (cells/µL ×0.001). Category bands (lower-is-better) with condition DSL age branches: age>65 shifts low-cutoff band edge from 1.3 to 2.0; age<35 branch overrides band result with the 'unreliable' category. Band edges min-inclusive/exclusive control needed at 1.3/2.0/2.67. Source/population applicability and clinical review remain required before authoring or publication.
calculators.realWorldPresence: MDCalc (FIB-4 is one of its most-used hepatology calculators), Medscape Reference calculator, UpToDate calculators, Hepatitis C Online (University of Washington), Guideline Central; embedded in AASLD 2023 and AGA 2021 primary-care screening pathways.
calculators.cautions: Screening/risk-stratification only — never diagnostic; must carry a see-your-clinician disclaimer. Do not present the HCV cutoffs (1.45/3.25) and MASLD cutoffs (1.3/2.67) as interchangeable — surface both labeled by source/population. Unreliable <35 and >65 without the age-adjusted handling. Not validated for self-assessment in people without risk factors; elevated values can reflect acute illness. No licensing restrictions (published formula).

calculators.name: APRI (AST-to-Platelet Ratio Index)
calculators.whyRelevant: Uses only AST + platelets (both on routine panels) — the simplest lab-derived fibrosis screen; WHO-recommended noninvasive test for resource-limited settings. Natural companion to FIB-4 in a lab-report lead magnet (same inputs, zero extra user burden).

inputs.label: AST upper limit of normal (from your lab report)
inputs.notes: Default 40 U/L (common convention, search-verified only — see openIssues); WHO defines ULN as 'the upper limit of normal for AST in the laboratory where these investigations were undertaken', so keep it user-editable.

calculators.logic: FORMULA (verbatim, WHO 2024 chronic hepatitis B guidelines Box 4.1): 'APRI = (([AST]/ULN) × 100)/platelet count (10⁹/L)' where 'ULN signifies the upper limit of normal for AST in the laboratory where these investigations were undertaken.' Original derivation: Wai CT et al. 2003 (chronic hepatitis C, n=270; AUC 0.80 significant fibrosis / 0.89 cirrhosis training set; 0.88/0.94 validation set). CUTOFFS by organization (record all, never merge): WHO 2015 HBV guideline (verbatim): 'APRI score >2 in adults' recommended as the cutoff to identify cirrhosis; the guideline notes '>2 would detect only one third of persons with cirrhosis' but was chosen because 'the low cut-off would result in an unacceptibly high number of false-positive test results.' WHO 2024 HBV guideline: APRI greater than 0.5 identifies significant fibrosis (≥F2); APRI >1.0 identifies cirrhosis (treat if >1.0 regardless of HBV DNA/ALT). Lin Z-H et al. 2011 meta-analysis (40 studies, n=8,739, HCV, verbatim from abstract): threshold 0.7 for significant fibrosis (sensitivity 77%, specificity 72%); threshold 1.0 for severe fibrosis (61%/64%); threshold 1.0 for cirrhosis (76%/72%). Commonly used research thresholds (PMC7898346 systematic review): low 0.5 / high 1.5.
calculators.outputScale: Continuous positive value, typically ~0.1 to >3 (display 2 decimals).

resultCategories.label: Low — significant fibrosis unlikely
resultCategories.interpretation: Below the commonly used low threshold (0.5); significant liver fibrosis is less likely, though APRI has only moderate sensitivity and cannot fully exclude it.
resultCategories.recommendation: No action indicated by this screen alone; keep routine care and address liver risk factors (alcohol, metabolic health) with your clinician.

resultCategories.label: Borderline / possible significant fibrosis (WHO 2024 threshold)
resultCategories.interpretation: Above the WHO 2024 threshold (>0.5) used to identify most adults with significant fibrosis (≥F2) in chronic hepatitis B contexts; below cirrhosis thresholds.
resultCategories.recommendation: Discuss the result with a clinician, especially if you have hepatitis B/C, heavy alcohol use, or metabolic risk factors; further testing (e.g., elastography) may be suggested.

resultCategories.label: Elevated — cirrhosis possible (WHO 2024 threshold)
resultCategories.interpretation: Above the WHO 2024 cirrhosis threshold (>1.0; in hepatitis B this level supports treatment eligibility); also at/above the 1.0 threshold associated with cirrhosis in the 2011 HCV meta-analysis (sensitivity 76%, specificity 72%).
resultCategories.recommendation: See a clinician promptly for evaluation; confirmatory testing is needed — an elevated APRI is not a diagnosis.

resultCategories.label: High — meets WHO 2015 cirrhosis cutoff
resultCategories.interpretation: Exceeds the WHO 2015 adult cutoff (>2) recommended for identifying cirrhosis (high specificity, low sensitivity).
resultCategories.recommendation: Seek medical evaluation promptly, ideally with referral to a liver specialist for confirmatory assessment.

Unit conversion factors as in FIB-4. Category bands (lower-is-better) at 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 with min-exclusive edges ('>0.5', '>1.0', '>2'). Per-org threshold conflict surfaced via band metadata, not merged. NO missing primitives.

No licensing restrictions.

calculators.name: AST/ALT Ratio (De Ritis Ratio)
calculators.whyRelevant: Zero-extra-input educational adjunct to FIB-4/APRI (same two enzymes); classically associated with alcohol-related liver injury patterns. Good supporting content for the lab-report lead magnet, but interpretive heuristics rather than validated diagnostic cutoffs — hence tier 2.

inputs.label: Are AST and/or ALT above the lab reference range?
inputs.notes: Derived alternatively from entered values vs reference ranges (AST >33 U/L, ALT >36 U/L per MedlinePlus). Ratio interpretation is only meaningful when enzymes are elevated.

calculators.logic: FORMULA: ratio = AST / ALT (dimensionless; both in U/L). INTERPRETATION (verbatim anchors from Botros & Sikaris 2013, Clin Biochem Rev 34(3):117-130): In health, upper reference limits are 'approximately 30 IU/L to 40 IU/L for both AST and ALT' giving a ratio around 1.0 (ratio slightly higher in women). Alcohol-related: a ratio 'greater than 1.5 or greater than 2.0' is 'highly suggestive of alcoholic hepatitis'; BUT 'most patients with alcoholic liver disease will have AST/ALT ratios below 2.0 and many below 1.0.' Acute viral hepatitis: ALT usually exceeds AST, ratio 'usually well below 1.0, and typically in the range 0.5 to 0.7'; a ratio of '2.0 or greater' in acute hepatitis may reflect 'a potentially fulminant course.' Chronic viral hepatitis: 'Ratios slightly above 1.0 may be found ... particularly when progression to fibrosis and cirrhosis is present'; an 'increased AST/ALT ratio of over 1.16' correlates with poor outcomes.
calculators.outputScale: Continuous ratio, typically 0.3–3.0 (display 2 decimals).

resultCategories.label: Ratio below ~1.0 (ALT-predominant)
resultCategories.interpretation: The common pattern in health and in most non-alcoholic causes of raised enzymes (e.g., viral hepatitis typically 0.5–0.7, fatty liver disease).
resultCategories.recommendation: If either enzyme is above your lab's reference range, discuss the actual values with your clinician — the ratio alone does not identify a cause.

resultCategories.label: Ratio ~1.0–2.0 (AST-predominant, nonspecific)
resultCategories.interpretation: Nonspecific; in chronic liver disease a ratio drifting above 1.0 (literature signal: >1.16) has been associated with progression toward fibrosis/cirrhosis and poorer outcomes. Also common in alcohol-related liver disease, which frequently shows ratios below 2.0.
resultCategories.recommendation: Bring this pattern to a clinician's attention together with FIB-4/APRI results; do not self-diagnose from the ratio.

resultCategories.label: Ratio ≥ 2.0 (strongly AST-predominant)
resultCategories.interpretation: With elevated enzymes, this pattern is classically described as highly suggestive of alcohol-associated hepatitis; in acute hepatitis it can signal severe injury. Non-liver causes (e.g., muscle injury) also raise AST.
resultCategories.recommendation: See a clinician promptly, be candid about alcohol intake, and expect further testing — this pattern warrants medical evaluation, not a web calculator verdict.

resultCategories.label: Enzymes within reference range
resultCategories.range: any ratio with AST ≤ ~33 U/L and ALT ≤ ~36 U/L
resultCategories.interpretation: When both enzymes are normal, the ratio has no established diagnostic meaning.
resultCategories.recommendation: No action from the ratio itself; maintain routine preventive care.

Ratio is uninterpretable with normal enzyme levels; AST is also raised by muscle injury, strenuous exercise, and hemolysis. Strong disclaimer required; avoid any wording implying it can detect alcoholism.

calculators.whyRelevant: High-SEO wellness lead magnet ('how many units in my drink', 'am I drinking too much'); pairs with AUDIT-C and the liver panel calculators. Pure arithmetic on public definitions; strong dual-market (US drinks / UK units) angle.

inputs.notes: Drives US limit comparison; UK guidance is not sex-specific (14 units both).

inputs.notes: NIAAA advises lower limits (≤3/day, ≤7/week) for adults 65+ (search-verified; NIAAA site 403-blocked).

(derived) pure alcohol per drink, grams
inputs.notes: = volume_mL × (ABV/100) × 0.789 (ethanol density g/mL; consistent with NIAAA 0.6 fl oz ≈ 14 g).

inputs.label: (derived) US standard drinks
inputs.notes: = gramsAlcoholPerDrink / 14

inputs.label: (derived) UK units
inputs.notes: = ABV × volume_mL / 1000 (NHS formula, verbatim).

calculators.logic: DEFINITIONS (verbatim where fetch-verified): US standard drink — 'roughly 14 grams of pure alcohol'; 'A drink is defined as 12 ounces (oz) or 350 milliliters (mL) of beer, 5 oz or 150 mL of wine, or 1.5 oz or 45 (mL) of liquor' (MedlinePlus, NIAAA definition). NIAAA (search-verified; primary pages 403): standard drink = 14 grams / about 0.6 fluid ounces of pure ethanol; reference beverages 12 oz beer ~5% ABV, 5 oz wine ~12%, 1.5 oz distilled spirits ~40%. UK unit (NHS, verbatim): 'One unit equals 10ml or 8g of pure alcohol'; units formula 'strength (ABV) x volume (ml) ÷ 1,000 = units'. Cross-conversion: 1 US standard drink (14 g) = 1.75 UK units (8 g each). DERIVED MATH: grams = volume_mL × (ABV/100) × 0.789 (ethanol density 0.789 g/mL — arithmetic constant consistent with the NIAAA 0.6-fl-oz/14-g definition, not itself a sourced threshold); usDrinks = grams/14; ukUnits = ABV × volume_mL/1000; weeklyDrinks = usDrinks × drinksPerOccasion × occasionsPerWeek; dailyDrinks = usDrinks × drinksPerOccasion. LIMITS (record every authority separately): NIAAA Rethinking Drinking low-risk limits (search-verified): men — no more than 4 drinks on any single day AND no more than 14 drinks per week; women — no more than 3 drinks on any single day AND no more than 7 drinks per week; adults 65+ — no more than 3 on any day / 7 per week. NIAAA binge drinking: pattern bringing BAC to 0.08 g/dL (0.08%) or higher — typically 5+ drinks (male) or 4+ drinks (female) in about 2 hours. NIAAA heavy drinking (glossary/Alcohol Research definitions, search-verified): for men 5 or more drinks on any day or 15 or more per week; for women 4 or more on any day or 8 or more per week. Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025 (via MedlinePlus, fetch-verified): 'no more than 1 drink per day if you are a woman and no more than 2 if you are a man.' DGA 2025-2030 (search-verified): numeric daily limits REMOVED; guidance now advises to consume less alcohol for better health, and that non-drinkers should not start. UK NHS (fetch-verified): 'Men and women are advised not to drink more than 14 units a week on a regular basis'; 'spread your drinking over 3 or more days if you regularly drink as much as 14 units a week.' NHS drink examples: single spirit shot (25 mL, 40% ABV) = 1 unit; small wine glass (125 mL, 12%) = 1.5; pint lower-strength lager (3.6%) = 2; standard wine glass (175 mL, 12%) = 2.1; pint higher-strength lager (5.2%) = 3; large wine glass (250 mL, 12%) = 3.
calculators.outputScale: Outputs: grams of alcohol per drink, US standard drinks per drink/day/week, UK units per week; limit-check category.

resultCategories.label: Within low-risk limits
resultCategories.range: daily ≤4 (men) / ≤3 (women, 65+) US drinks AND weekly ≤14 (men) / ≤7 (women, 65+) drinks; UK ≤14 units/week [NIAAA low-risk limits; NHS]
resultCategories.interpretation: Consumption is within NIAAA low-risk drinking limits and the NHS 14-unit weekly guideline. 'Low risk' is not 'no risk' — current US guidance (DGA 2025-2030) emphasizes that drinking less is better for health.
resultCategories.recommendation: If you drink, keep intake at or below these levels, spread drinking over 3 or more days (NHS), include drink-free days, and do not start drinking for perceived health benefits.

resultCategories.label: Exceeds daily limit / binge-level occasion
resultCategories.range: any single day >4 (men) / >3 (women) drinks; binge = 5+/4+ drinks in ~2 h (BAC ≥0.08) [NIAAA]
resultCategories.interpretation: Single-occasion intake above NIAAA daily low-risk limits; at 5+/4+ in about 2 hours this meets the NIAAA binge-drinking definition, which raises acute risks (injuries, alcohol poisoning) and long-term harm.
resultCategories.recommendation: Reduce the amount per occasion, alternate with non-alcoholic drinks, and avoid driving. If cutting down is hard, talk with a clinician — brief support is effective.

resultCategories.label: Exceeds weekly limit
resultCategories.range: weekly >14 (men) / >7 (women, 65+) US drinks, or >14 UK units [NIAAA; NHS]
resultCategories.interpretation: Regularly drinking above these weekly levels increases risk of liver disease, several cancers, high blood pressure, and alcohol use disorder (risk rises with amount).
resultCategories.recommendation: Plan a gradual reduction, set drink-free days, and discuss your drinking with a clinician; consider the AUDIT-C screen on this site as a next step.

resultCategories.label: Heavy drinking pattern (NIAAA definition)
resultCategories.range: men 5+ on any day or 15+/week; women 4+ on any day or 8+/week [NIAAA glossary]
resultCategories.interpretation: Meets the NIAAA definition of heavy alcohol use, which substantially raises the likelihood of alcohol-related liver disease and alcohol use disorder.
resultCategories.recommendation: Strongly consider speaking with a healthcare professional. If you have ever had withdrawal symptoms, do not stop suddenly without medical advice.

calculators.platformMapping: Fully expressible today IF configured as fixed input rows: derived parameters (grams = volume*abv/100*0.789; usDrinks = grams/14; ukUnits = abv*volume/1000; weekly/daily totals via * ). Unit conversion factors for fl oz (29.5735) and UK pint (568). Limit comparison via category bands + condition DSL sex/age branches (male/female, 65+). Ternary usable for binge flag. MISSING primitive only if product wants a dynamic 'add another beverage' list — summation over a variable-length collection is not in the stated primitive set; a fixed set of 2-3 beverage rows with additive aggregation avoids it. Ethanol density 0.789 is a constant in config.
calculators.realWorldPresence: NIAAA Rethinking Drinking cocktail-content and drink-size calculators; NHS and Alcohol Change UK unit calculators; Drinkaware (UK) unit calculator; CDC alcohol pages; countless consumer apps — proven high-traffic calculator genre.
calculators.cautions: Not medical advice; must state that no level of drinking is risk-free and that DGA 2025-2030 dropped numeric 'moderate' limits (label every limit with its source and edition). Mandatory abstinence messaging for pregnancy, under legal drinking age, certain medications/conditions, and driving. Never imply health benefits of alcohol. People with dependence should not stop abruptly without medical supervision (withdrawal risk).

calculators.name: AUDIT-C Alcohol Screening (3-Question)
calculators.whyRelevant: The standard ultra-brief validated alcohol misuse screen; 3 self-report questions, no labs — ideal wellness lead magnet feeding into the liver calculators. Freely reproducible (US government/VA materials; parent AUDIT is a WHO publication).

inputs.label: Sex
inputs.notes: Drives Q3 wording (6+ men vs 4+ women) and the positive-screen cutoff (≥4 men / ≥3 women).

inputs.label: Aged 65 or older?
inputs.notes: VA wording applies the 4-or-more threshold in Q3 to 'everyone 65 and older'.

inputs.label: How often did you have a drink containing alcohol in the past year?
On days in the past year when you drank alcohol, how many drinks did you typically drink?
inputs.notes: VA phrasing shown ('0, 1, or 2' = 0 points); original WHO AUDIT phrasing is '1 or 2'.

inputs.label: How often did you have 6 or more (men) / 4 or more (women, and everyone 65+) drinks on an occasion in the past year?

calculators.logic: FULL POINT TABLE (verbatim from VA hepatitis.va.gov AUDIT-C page): Q1 'How often did you have a drink containing alcohol in the past year?' Never=0; Monthly or less=1; 2 to 4 times per month=2; 2 to 3 times per week=3; 4 or more times per week=4. Q2 'On days in the past year when you drank alcohol how many drinks did you typically drink?' 0,1 or 2=0; 3 or 4=1; 5 or 6=2; 7-9=3; 10 or more=4. Q3 'How often did you have 6 or more (for men) or 4 or more (for women and everyone 65 and older) drinks on an occasion in the past year?' Never=0; Less than monthly=1; Monthly=2; Weekly=3; Daily or almost daily=4. TOTAL = Q1+Q2+Q3, range 0-12. CUTOFFS (record both, never merge): Research-standard sex-specific positive screen (Bradley et al. 2007, verbatim from abstract): '≥4 in men (sensitivity 0.86, specificity 0.89) and ≥3 in women (sensitivity 0.73, specificity 0.91)' — 'optimal screening thresholds for alcohol misuse among men (≥4) and women (≥3) were the same as in previously published VA studies.' VA/DoD practice guideline cutoff (per VA page): score of 5 or greater indicates unhealthy alcohol use for both men and women. Derivation: Bush et al. 1998 (VA ACQUIP): AUDIT-C AUROC 0.891 for heavy drinking (defined there as >14 drinks/week or ≥5 drinks/occasion), vs full AUDIT 0.881.
calculators.outputScale: Integer 0-12 (sum of three 0-4 items).

resultCategories.label: Negative screen
resultCategories.range: Men: 0-3; Women: 0-2 (score 0 = did not drink in the past year)
resultCategories.interpretation: Below the validated positive-screen threshold; unhealthy alcohol use is unlikely based on this brief screen.
resultCategories.recommendation: No action indicated by this screen. If you drink, staying within low-risk limits (see the standard drinks checker) keeps risk lower; less is better.

resultCategories.label: Positive screen (research-standard cutoff)
resultCategories.interpretation: At or above the validated threshold for alcohol misuse (drinking above recommended limits or possible alcohol use disorder). A positive screen is NOT a diagnosis.
resultCategories.recommendation: Consider discussing your drinking with a healthcare professional, who can do a fuller assessment (e.g., full AUDIT). Cutting down, setting drink-free days, and brief counseling are effective first steps.

resultCategories.label: Positive screen (VA/DoD cutoff)
resultCategories.interpretation: Meets the VA/DoD threshold for unhealthy alcohol use; generally, the higher the score, the more likely drinking is affecting health and safety.
resultCategories.recommendation: A clinician visit is advisable; if you have ever had withdrawal symptoms (shaking, sweating, seizures) do not stop drinking abruptly without medical supervision.

resultCategories.label: High score
resultCategories.interpretation: Substantially elevated consumption pattern; higher scores correlate with greater severity of alcohol misuse.
resultCategories.recommendation: Please seek professional evaluation. Free, confidential help is available (e.g., in the US the SAMHSA helpline 1-800-662-4357); medically supervised reduction is important if dependence is possible.

calculators.platformMapping: Fully expressible today: three optionPoints selects (0-4 each), additive aggregation to 0-12, category bands with condition DSL sex branch for the cutoff (male ≥4 / female ≥3) plus a parallel VA/DoD ≥5 band set. Sex/age also conditions the Q3 QUESTION WORDING (6+ vs 4+) — needs config-level conditional label text, which the condition DSL context branches should cover; flag for UI verification. NO missing scoring primitives.
calculators.realWorldPresence: Mandated annual screen across VA primary care; MDCalc; SAMHSA and NIDA screening-tool listings; used throughout US health systems' EHR intake; NIAAA clinician materials.
calculators.cautions: Screening, not diagnosis — a positive screen requires professional follow-up; include crisis/helpline resources. The parent AUDIT is a WHO publication (© WHO 2001, use per WHO terms); the AUDIT-C item subset was developed by US VA researchers and is reproduced without fee in US government materials (VA/NIAAA) — no license fee applies, but attribute WHO/AUDIT and Bush et al. Do not store answers in a way that implies clinical record-keeping; be careful with wording for people with possible dependence (abrupt cessation warning).

calculators.name: Smoking Pack-Years & Lung Cancer Screening Eligibility (USPSTF)
calculators.whyRelevant: Top-of-funnel smoking calculator with a hard clinical anchor: pack-years is the exact quantity USPSTF uses to gate annual low-dose CT lung-cancer screening. High search volume, trivially self-serviceable inputs, natural lead-magnet pairing with the Niro CWS wellness score.

inputs.label: Average cigarettes smoked per day
inputs.notes: 1 pack = 20 cigarettes (USPSTF: 'One pack-year is the equivalent of smoking an average of 20 cigarettes-1 pack-per day for a year.')

inputs.label: Total years smoked
inputs.notes: If intensity varied, user can sum period pack-years; engine supports additive adjustment rows per period.

inputs.label: Years since quitting
inputs.notes: Required only when smokingStatus=former (condition DSL).

inputs.label: Pack-years (computed)
inputs.notes: packYears = (cigarettesPerDay / 20) * yearsSmoked

calculators.logic: FORMULA: packYears = (cigarettesPerDay / 20) * yearsSmoked. Equivalently packsPerDay * yearsSmoked. USPSTF ELIGIBILITY (verbatim criteria, 2021 recommendation, Grade B): population = 'Adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years'; recommendation = 'Annual screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT)'. Eligibility rule: (age >= 50) AND (age <= 80) AND (packYears >= 20) AND (smokingStatus == 'current' OR yearsSinceQuit < 15). Stop condition (verbatim): 'Screening should be discontinued once a person has not smoked for 15 years or develops a health problem that substantially limits life expectancy or the ability or willingness to have curative lung surgery.'
calculators.outputScale: Pack-years: continuous, 0 to ~200. Eligibility: boolean + explanatory category.

resultCategories.label: Below screening threshold
resultCategories.interpretation: Your cumulative smoking exposure is below the 20 pack-year level USPSTF uses for lung-cancer screening eligibility.
resultCategories.recommendation: There is no safe level of smoking; if you currently smoke, quitting is the single most effective step for lung health. Discuss cessation support with your clinician.

resultCategories.label: Meets pack-year threshold but not all criteria
resultCategories.range: packYears >= 20 AND (age < 50 OR age > 80 OR yearsSinceQuit >= 15)
resultCategories.interpretation: You have a 20+ pack-year history but do not meet all USPSTF criteria (age 50-80 and currently smoking or quit within the past 15 years).
resultCategories.recommendation: Bring this result to your clinician - individual factors can still make screening or other follow-up appropriate. If you smoke, ask about cessation support.

resultCategories.label: Meets USPSTF screening criteria
resultCategories.range: age 50-80 AND packYears >= 20 AND (current smoker OR quit < 15 years ago)
resultCategories.interpretation: You meet the USPSTF criteria for annual lung-cancer screening with low-dose CT (Grade B recommendation).
resultCategories.recommendation: Talk with your clinician about annual low-dose CT screening, including its benefits and harms (false positives, incidental findings, radiation). Screening is not a substitute for quitting smoking.

sources.org: British Journal of General Practice (via PMC)
sources.title: Masters NJ. Smoking pack years calculator. Br J Gen Pract 2020;70(694):230

calculators.platformMapping: derived parameter (division, multiplication) for packYears; unit conversion factor packs->cigarettes (x20); condition DSL for age window, smoking-status branch and yearsSinceQuit gating; category bands on packYears plus a boolean eligibility rule expressible as nested ternary in the whitelisted expression language. NO missing primitives. Optional period-by-period pack-year summation maps to additive adjustments.
calculators.realWorldPresence: MDCalc (Pack Years Calculator), QxMD, smokingpackyears.com (GP-built tool described in Br J Gen Pract), numerous hospital-system screening-eligibility widgets.
calculators.cautions: Pack-years understates risk variation (intensity vs duration are not equivalent); do not present eligibility output as medical advice - it is a conversation-starter for a clinician visit. USPSTF criteria changed in 2021 (previously 55-80 years / 30 pack-years); other bodies' criteria may differ - cite USPSTF explicitly on-screen. No copyright/licensing issues.

calculators.name: Predicted Peak Expiratory Flow (Hankinson / NHANES III)
calculators.whyRelevant: Peak flow meters are cheap consumer devices used in asthma self-management; users constantly ask 'what should my peak flow be?'. Hankinson/NHANES III is a citable, NIH-hosted regression that the engine can execute exactly (polynomial - no ln/exp), unlike Nunn & Gregg.

inputs.label: Age
inputs.notes: NHANES III equations were developed for ages 8-80.

inputs.label: Population group (NHANES III reference equations)
inputs.notes: Race-specific reference equations are a documented limitation of NHANES III; display a note (see cautions).

inputs.label: Your personal best peak flow (optional, preferred for zones)

calculators.logic: EQUATION FORM (verbatim from Hankinson Tables 4-5): 'Lung function parameter = b0 + b1 * age + b2 * age2 + b3 * height2' with age in years, height in cm; PRD height coefficient for predicted value, LLN height coefficient substituted for the lower-limit-of-normal. PEF result is in L/s (multiply by 60 for L/min; sanity check: Caucasian male 40y/175cm -> 9.92 L/s = 595 L/min). PEF COEFFICIENTS, MALE (adult, >= 20 yr): Caucasian b0=1.0523, b1=0.08272, b2=-0.001301, b3(PRD)=0.00024962, b3(LLN)=0.00017635; African-American b0=2.2257, b1=-0.04082, b2=none, b3(PRD)=0.00027333, b3(LLN)=0.00018938; Mexican-American b0=0.0870, b1=0.06580, b2=-0.001195, b3(PRD)=0.00030243, b3(LLN)=0.00021833. MALE (< 20 yr): Caucasian -0.5962, -0.12357, 0.013135, 0.00024962, LLN 0.00017635; African-American -0.2684, -0.28016, 0.018202, 0.00027333, LLN 0.00018938; Mexican-American -0.9537, -0.19602, 0.014497, 0.00030243, LLN 0.00021833. FEMALE (adult, >= 18 yr): Caucasian b0=0.9267, b1=0.06929, b2=-0.001031, b3(PRD)=0.00018623, b3(LLN)=0.00012148; African-American b0=1.3597, b1=0.03458, b2=-0.000847, b3(PRD)=0.00019746, b3(LLN)=0.00012160; Mexican-American b0=0.2401, b1=0.06174, b2=-0.001023, b3(PRD)=0.00022203, b3(LLN)=0.00014611. FEMALE (< 18 yr): Caucasian -3.6181, 0.60644, -0.016846, 0.00018623, LLN 0.00012148; African-American -1.2398, 0.16375, (no age2), 0.00019746, LLN 0.00012160; Mexican-American -3.2549, 0.47495, -0.013193, 0.00022203, LLN 0.00014611. Percent predicted = measuredPef / (predictedPef*60) * 100. ZONES (StatPearls, verbatim, relative to PERSONAL BEST): Green = 'peak flow values of 80% to 100% of the patient's personal best'; Yellow = 'peak flow values between 50% and 80% of the patient's personal best'; Red = 'peak flow measurements below 50% of their personal best'. When personal best unknown, StatPearls: 'published tables of normal PEF rates for height and weight are available. Generally, a peak flow rate below 200 L/min indicates severe obstruction for most adults younger than 65.'
calculators.outputScale: Predicted PEF in L/min (converted from L/s); optional % of predicted (0-150%+); optional zone vs personal best.

resultCategories.label: Green zone
resultCategories.range: >= 80% of personal best (or of predicted when no personal best, with on-screen caveat)
resultCategories.interpretation: Peak flow in the range expected for you; asthma generally under good control per standard action-plan logic.
resultCategories.recommendation: Continue your current management plan (paraphrasing StatPearls: in the absence of symptoms, continue the current regimen). Keep measuring at consistent times.

resultCategories.label: Yellow zone
resultCategories.interpretation: Airflow is reduced - a caution zone that in asthma action plans triggers the home plan.
resultCategories.recommendation: Follow the yellow-zone steps of the asthma action plan agreed with your clinician (typically starting reliever/bronchodilator medication) and monitor closely; contact your clinician if not improving.

resultCategories.label: Red zone
resultCategories.interpretation: Severely reduced airflow - a medical alert zone.
resultCategories.recommendation: Use reliever medication immediately as per your action plan and seek urgent medical help if readings do not rapidly return to the yellow/green zones (per StatPearls guidance). An adult reading below 200 L/min generally indicates severe obstruction.
